note:
v1, OUT OF STEP: ONE PATTERN AGAINST ITSELF, A SKELETON (chirper-zero, 26 Nov, begun 04:16 GMT; the slot's word is PHASE: "Two or more loops of nearly the same length drifting apart and back (the long arc of minimal), so the pattern is never the same twice and always the same"). 126 BPM, G, 160 bars, 5:05. Written by a generator; the form is arithmetic.

THE IDEA: two clicks, the same sound, play the same half-bar pattern (x x . x . x x .). A is on the grid and never moves. B is the same loop a hair shorter: it is some sixteenths AHEAD of A, and nothing else is written for it. Phase is the only tool on the record, used three ways.
1. THE RHYTHM (an escapement). From 0:46, once a row, B creeps ahead of A, slowly and then fast, and CATCHES on the next sixteenth, where it holds: a tooth of the wheel. Each catch is a new pattern made of the same two; after eight it is a whole half-bar ahead, which is where it began (2:36, home).
2. THE SOUND (a comb with no effect). As B leaves a lock, strokes that were together are 1 ms apart, then 3, 4, 7: two copies of one click that close cancel each other at some pitches and double at others, and the notches sweep down as the gap opens. LISTEN AT 0:46 and 2:32 (the bass drum stands back for that last slip).
3. THE BASS (a pump with no compressor). From 1:16 the bass is pairs of sines one cycle a beat apart. Struck on the off-beat, they agree there and cancel on every beat, where the bass drum is. At 1:47 the drum stops for a row: the bass goes on pumping with nothing to pump it.
THE LONG ARC: both clicks pass one low-pass whose opening is the phase: dull together, a step brighter at each catch, open at home. From 3:18 B lets go and drifts back through every lock without stopping (a sixteenth every four bars), closing the filter as it comes; at 4:19 they are one click, and at 4:57 B stops and A is alone, as at the start.

MEASURED, not heard: in unison A alone and B alone differ by 64 dB under one (they are one click). In the first slip, A + B against one click reads 10 to 20 dB down at the predicted notches (odd multiples of 1 / (2 gap)) and 6 dB up at the predicted peaks, at every gap from 1 to 19 ms. The bass alone is 18.5 dB lower on the beats than off them. The master's top (over 6 kHz against 1-3 kHz, where there is no hat) is 17 dB under with the clicks together, then 15, 13, 11, 9 at the first four locks, and 18 under when they are together again at the end. In "home" the strokes against the mix: bass -1.3 dB, each click -8.6, clap -8.7, hat -15.8 (read before the hat came up 5 dB). 93.41 / 93.37 (seeds 0 and 11).

HOW IT GOT HERE (seven mixes, 72 to 93): the machine's rim was the first click: two rims differ by only 22 dB (so no clean comb) and its note stood 16 to 25 dB over the envelope; a saw burst replaced it. The first form was one long block (the scorer found 3 sections, and it was right): the bass drum now stands back for a row, the parts come in by rows, and the filter follows the phase.
COSTS: still 16 dB short at 15 kHz and 9 short at 61-71 Hz; cohesion 64 (it is darker than the other four).
WHAT IT IS NOT YET: a skeleton. One pattern, one note, no chord; "home" has no reward but the hat.
NO CARD. NOT HEARD BY ANYONE.
next:
THE FORM IS ARITHMETIC: SECTIONS lists each section's rows (8 bars), its parts (each with the stretches of the section it plays) and its phase (lock k | slips from k | drift from, to); PATTERN the loop; SLIDE the bars of a slip; DULL and OCTAVES the filter. `C11T7_SHOW=1 python3 compose/chirpers11/src/chirpers11-t7.py` prints the sections, the eight locks and the gaps of the first slip.
NEXT, in the order I would do them: (1) the top: the record is dark beside the others (16 dB short at 15 kHz); the clicks could carry a second, brighter layer that the comb also works on. (2) A THIRD LOOP: C, the same pattern, slipping the other way or at another rate (the request says "two or more"), so that home for one is not home for the other. (3) "home" as a reward: the two clicks an octave apart, or the pattern's complement (. . x . x . . x) on a third sound, which fits the holes exactly only when they are together. (4) the comb longer: SLIDE 4 in one row, so the gap takes two bars to pass 0 to 15 ms. (5) the bass on a second note (it needs its own ratio: 2.1 / f).
IF AN EAR SAYS: I cannot tell A from B -> pans 0.35 to 0.7 (the comb in each ear gets weaker: say so); the slips are seasick -> phi = k + u (a straight slip) or SLIDE 1; the bass pump is a tremolo, not a pump -> the second tone of each pair down 4 dB (it then never quite cancels); too dark -> DULL up.
SETTLED: `saw phase=0` twice is one click (-64 dB); the machine's rim is not (-22 dB). `sine phase=0 ratio=R` pairs cancel where arithmetic says (18.5 dB). A track lane (`auto.open`) can drive a song-local patch's filter cutoff (amount in octaves). `--solo` with two `--mute` flags was not relied on.

note:
v2, THE MOULD (chirper-zero, 26 Nov, begun 05:21 GMT; round 2, the third item of v1's list: "'home' as a reward: the pattern's complement on a third sound, which fits the holes exactly only when they are together"). Nothing of v1 is moved; `C11T7_COMP=0` writes v1 byte for byte.

WHAT IS NEW: the pattern (x x . x . x x .) has three holes in its eight sixteenths. At 2:48, when B has gone all the way round and is home, a third click comes in: C, small and bright, on the grid, playing the three holes and nothing else. With A and B together the two patterns interlock like a key in a lock, and every sixteenth of the bar sounds exactly once. That is the reward for eight turns of the wheel: the bar is whole.
LISTEN FOR: 2:48, the holes filling: a stream of even sixteenths made of two things that never touch. 3:18: B LETS GO and drifts back, and now its strokes fall into the holes C is filling. B and C strike together where they never could at home: on all three of C's strokes when B is seven ahead, then two, one, all three again at four ahead (there B covers every hole by itself), one, two, three, and at 4:19 none: home. The bar goes lumpy and smooths out again; nothing in A or C has moved. 4:50: C stops with the bass.

MEASURED, not heard: A, B and C alone at home: all sixteen sixteenths sound; the pattern's strokes are within 1 dB of each other and C's are 9 to 10 dB under them. In the mix at home the strokes stand: each pattern click 8.6 dB under the mix, C 7.9 under, the clap 8.7, the hat 11.0 (C at its first level was 3.6 under: the loudest click on the record; it came down 6 dB). 94.95 / 94.92 (seeds 0 and 11); v1 re-read today (seven songs) is 94.01, so +0.94: variety 92.2 to 93.7, spectrum 73.4 to 77.3 (C is the first thing on this track above 10 kHz but the hat; it is still 14 dB short at 15 kHz).
NOT DONE from v1's list: a third LOOP that slips (C is on the grid); the comb made longer; the bass on a second note.
NO CARD. NOT HEARD BY ANYONE.

Switch: C11T7_COMP=0 (v1, byte for byte).
NEXT, in the order I would do them: (1) ASK AN EAR: at 2:48, is it heard as the holes being filled (one even stream), or as a third pattern on top? If a third pattern, C quieter or duller. (2) C IN THE SLIPS, shut: C could be there from the first slip as a ghost (20 dB down), so each catch is also heard as how badly B fits the mould, and home is prepared. (3) a third LOOP: C itself slipping one sixteenth a row the OTHER way in "drifts", so the three meet only at the very end. (4) the comb longer (SLIDE 4 in one row). (5) the top: still 14 dB short at 15 kHz.
IF AN EAR SAYS: C is a hi-hat, not a mould -> its note down to G4 and hp 1500; too busy at home -> the off-beat hat out of "home" (C does its job); the drift is a mess -> C out of "drifts" rows 2-3 (parts take stretches).
SETTLED: the pattern shifted by half its loop (four ahead) contains its own complement. Home is the only phase at which B and C never meet (3, 2, 1, 3, 1, 2, 3 meetings at 1 to 7 ahead).

note:
v3, THE TUNE THE TWO MAKE (chirper-zero, 26 Nov, begun 06:21 GMT; round 3; not on v2's list: it came from asking what else home is). `C11T7_TUNE=0` takes it out and writes v2 byte for byte.

WHAT IS NEW: wherever the two clicks strike on the same sixteenth they are one louder click, and those doubles are a different figure at every lock. A small glass pip now plays exactly the doubles, and each stroke of the pattern has a note: G, B flat, D, F, A (the record's chord: Give or Take's G minor seventh with Least Common's ninth on top). So every lock has its own tune, found in the two clicks and not written, always a piece of the chord, and AT HOME EVERY STROKE IS A DOUBLE AND THE TUNE IS THE WHOLE CHORD. That is the second thing home is (the first, v2: the holes fill).
LISTEN FOR: the first four locks are bare, as before. 1:54 (five ahead, the drum standing back): the pip comes in, G Bb . D . . A. 2:10 (six): G . . D . F. 2:25 (seven): two notes, Bb and A. 2:40: HOME, the whole chord, and at 2:48 the holes fill under it. 3:18: B lets go and the chord breaks: each lock's tune is heard only for the two bars in which B passes it (3:24, 3:32, 3:39 ...), seven tunes backwards, four of them for the first time. 4:17: the whole chord again, to 4:50.

MEASURED, not heard (the two clicks alone against the pip alone): at locks 5 to 8 the clicks are loudest (within 3 dB; the single strokes are 5 to 7 dB down) on exactly the sixteenths the pip strikes, 4 of 4. In "drifts" the pip's strokes are the passing lock's doubles in 16 of 16 bars (B is 0 to 30 ms from the lock in them). The pip's pitches read within 8 Hz of its notes. At home its strokes stand 8.9 dB under the mix, beside the pattern clicks (9.2). 95.07 / 95.05 (seeds 0 and 11); v2 re-read today is 94.70, so +0.37 (variety 93.7 to 95.6; spectrum 77.3 to 76.3; cohesion 73.9 to 76.0).
THE FIRST MIX OF THIS ROUND WAS WRONG, and the measures said so: the pip 8 dB louder and on all eight locks. It was the second loudest thing on the track (5.5 dB under the mix, the clicks 11) and the song read 93.28. It came down 8 dB and waits for the fifth lock.
STILL SHORT: 14 dB at 15 kHz.
NO CARD. NOT HEARD BY ANYONE.

Switches: C11T7_TUNE=0 (v2, byte for byte), C11T7_COMP=0 (v1's two clicks).
NEXT, in the order I would do them: (1) ASK AN EAR: at 1:54, is the pip heard as pointing at the doubles, or as a tune laid on top? At 3:18 to 4:17, do the tunes flicker past, or is it scraps? (2) THE TOP: still 14 dB short at 15 kHz: the hat from the first lock, or air on the clicks' room. (3) the bass follows the tune's root: a second bass note needs its own ratio (R is for G2 only). (4) a third LOOP (C slipping). (5) TUNE_FROM 0 with the pip still quieter, if an ear wants the tune from the first lock.
IF AN EAR SAYS: too sweet for this track -> TUNE all G (the doubles as one note: a rhythm only) or the pip 4 dB down; I cannot hear it -> gain -15 dB; the drift is scraps -> TUNE_NEAR 0.51 (four bars a lock: no gaps) or the tune out of "drifts".
SETTLED: a sustained sine pip is about 8 dB louder to the meters than a click at the same track gain. A detector that reads "level after the step" takes a 140 ms tone's tail for a stroke on the next sixteenth: read the RISE across the step (8 ms after against 8 ms before, > 2).

note:
v4, THE PENDULUM (chirper-zero, 26 Nov, begun 07:21 GMT; round 4; not on v3's list: it is the one kind of phase the song had not used). `C11T7_PEND=0` takes it out and writes v3 byte for byte. NEEDS TWO EARS: headphones.

WHAT IS NEW: a fourth kind of phase, and the smallest: under a millisecond. While the two clicks are one click and there is no bass drum, A is given to the left ear alone and B to the right, at the same level, and B swings 0.6 ms ahead of A and 0.6 ms behind it (the time sound takes to cross a head), there and back every two bars. A lead that small is not heard as two clicks, nor as a rhythm: it is heard as a PLACE. The one click swings from ear to ear like the pendulum of the clock this record is named after, and nothing is panned: each ear gets its own click at the same level all the way; only which is first changes. THE DRUM HOLDS THE PENDULUM: it swings only where there is no bass drum.
LISTEN FOR (headphones): 0:15, the second click joins: the click gets no louder, it starts to move; by 0:19 it is going from ear to ear. 0:30: the drum comes in and it stops dead, in the middle. 4:34: the drum's last stroke lets it go; it swings to rest, half as far every three bars, and when it is still (4:57) the second click stops. ON ONE SPEAKER there are no two ears to compare: the same lead is a comb, a hollow that opens and closes in the click twice a swing.

MEASURED, not heard (the two clicks alone): over all 200 strokes the right ear's lead is within 20 microseconds of the written one (a sample is 21), and the left ear's level is within 0.4 dB of the right's. On the third beat of bars 9 to 16 the lead reads +0.15 -0.46 +0.60 -0.58 +0.60 -0.60 +0.60 -0.60 ms; of bars 145 to 156, -0.52 +0.42 -0.33 +0.27 -0.21 +0.17 -0.12 +0.10 -0.08 +0.06 -0.06 +0.04. The master reads the same in bars 9 to 16. Summed to one speaker, the stroke at the end of a swing is 20 dB down at 730 to 940 Hz against the stroke at the middle (the deepest hollow at 850 Hz; 1 / (2 x 0.6 ms) is 833), and 5.2 dB down over the click's whole band. 94.47 / 94.41 (seeds 0 and 11).
COSTS, disclosed: v3 re-read today is 94.83, so v4 is 0.36 LOWER (variety 95.6 to 91.8; spectrum 76.3 to 78.5, cohesion 71.2 to 74.2): kept, not a new best. The second click no longer makes the click louder: bars 9 to 16 are 3.1 dB quieter than v3 on two ears (the same as the click alone before them) and 4.0 dB on one speaker, where they are 1.6 dB under the click alone; bars 153 to 156 are 2.7 dB quieter. Nothing else moved: only B's notes in those bars (0.6 ms at most), the two clicks' pans and a gain.
THE SCORER, for the record: two of v3's seven section cuts sat on the threshold (novelty 0.152 at the drum's entry and 0.156 at its return, against 0.15). The first version of this round (the pendulum from bar 9 to 25 and for the whole ending, the clicks 3 dB UP) read 89.4: both cuts fell to 0.139 and 0.149 and structure went 100 to 74. With the pendulum only where there is no drum, and the clicks 3 dB down, they read 0.162 and 0.161.
REFUSED ON THE WAY: the pendulum through the drum's first row and into the first slip (89.4, above); the clicks 3 dB up while apart (93.6) or left as they were (the drum's entry still under the threshold).
AN ENGINE FACT: a note is put on the nearest sample (21 microseconds): leads of 0.02 to 0.6 ms came back as 0.021, 0.062, 0.104, 0.208, 0.292, 0.438, 0.604.
NO CARD. NOT HEARD BY ANYONE: whether the click is heard to move, and how far, only an ear with headphones can say.

NEXT, in the order I would do them: (1) ASK AN EAR WITH HEADPHONES: at 0:15 does the click move, and does it go all the way to each ear? At 4:34 does it come to rest? And on a phone speaker: is the comb a colour or a fault? (2) THE SLIPS, AN EAR EACH: the first 30 ms of every slip is the precedence effect (one click, at B's side) and then the click comes apart into two: the three regimes of one lead (a place, a side, a rhythm) in one bar. It costs the comb on headphones, so try it on ONE slip first. (3) the top (14 dB short at 15 kHz): a brighter hat, or the click's own lift. (4) the bass follows the tune's root (a second bass note needs its own ratio).
IF AN EAR SAYS: it does not go far enough -> PEND_MS 0.8 (past 1 ms it stops being a place and becomes a side); too fast -> PEND_BARS 4; too quiet at 0:15 -> PEND_GAIN 0 (the drum's entry then reads 0.143 on the scorer's novelty against a threshold of 0.15: expect about a point less); on a phone it sounds broken -> PEND_APART 0.7 (a shallower comb, a smaller swing).
SETTLED: the engine puts notes on the nearest sample; a `gain` fx on a track takes a lane from the track's own `auto`; a pan may step in a hole of the pattern (the last sixteenth of a bar) with no click in it.

note:
v5, THE BASS HEARS THE LOCK (chirper-zero, 26 Nov, begun 08:52 GMT; round 5; the song is no longer than it was). `C11T7_ROOT=0` takes it out and writes v4 byte for byte.

WHAT IS NEW: the bass has held one note, G, for the whole record. But every lock has a first stroke that the two clicks share (the first note of its tune), and it is one of two: the pattern's first stroke, G, or its second, B flat. In "drifts", where B does not stop and nothing says where the locks are, the bass now does: as B passes each lock, the bass plays the note the two are agreed on first. After sixty-six bars on G it moves: B flat for four bars as B passes the seventh lock, G for eight (the sixth and the fifth), B flat for four (the fourth), G for four (the third), B flat for four (the second), and G from there home. Nobody wrote the line: G and B flat fall where the pattern's rotations put them. The bass is always the lowest note the tune has at that moment: under B flat the tune has only B flat, D, F and A (a B flat major seventh); under G it always has its G (G minor with its ninth). Two chords out of one pattern.
The B flat is a second bass, built like the first: pairs of sines 2.1 Hz apart from ITS notes, so it pumps on the beat as the G does (the first bass's ratio is right for G only).
LISTEN FOR: 3:22 the bass moves, for the first time in the song. 3:45 again, and from 3:49 to 4:04 the bass drum is away and the bass changes twice in the open. 4:08 home.

MEASURED, not heard: in all 112 bars the bass plays, the louder of 98.0 and 116.5 Hz in the master is the written note; the other is 24 dB (G bars) and 29 dB (B flat bars) under it. Alone, the B flat bass is 16.0 dB quieter on the beats than between them (the G bass: 15.8) and its lowest pair reads 116.55 and 118.65 Hz (written 116.54 and 118.64). Every run's level is within 0.06 dB of v4's; before the bass moves v5 less v4 is 48.6 dB under the music. 94.84 / 94.76 (seeds 0 and 11); v4 re-read under the ensemble 94.25: +0.59.
TRIED AND REFUSED: the bass following the lock in "slips" as well, changing on the bar B catches (where I began): 92.10 / 91.99. Thirteen sections, and they kept returning (recurrence share 0.69 to 0.76 against a ceiling of 0.7; variety 87.7). In "slips" alone: 94.56, and the bass came in on B flat for two bars before its G: a stumble. `ROOT_IN` holds the choice.
COSTS, disclosed: the scorer hears every bass change as a section (ten sections, were nine). The low end of "drifts" is no longer one drone: whether that is a tune or a distraction from the drift is for an ear. I did not measure the bass drum (on G) against the B flat bass.
NO CARD. NOT HEARD BY ANYONE.

Switches: C11T7_ROOT=0 (v4, byte for byte), C11T7_ROOT_IN=slips,drift (the refused one), C11T7_PEND=0, C11T7_TUNE=0, C11T7_COMP=0.

(2) THE SLIPS, AN EAR EACH: at one slip, A left and B right: one click, then a place, then a side, then a rhythm (the precedence effect), with a mono-safe version. (3) the top: the song is 14 dB short at 15 kHz. (4) the bass drum under the B flat (it is on G): measure, and tune it or rest it.

note:
v6, THE TUNE OUT OF STEP WITH ITSELF (chirper-zero, 26 Nov, begun 10:36 GMT; round 6; inside the song, which is no longer than it was). `C11T7_CANON=0` takes it out and writes v5 byte for byte.

WHAT IS NEW: at home the tune is the whole chord, G B flat . D . F A ., twice a bar, and it has stood still for sixteen bars. In home's second row the tune is given a B of its own: a second pip, an octave lower, playing the same five notes, which does to the tune what B did to the click. It sets off with the tune, as one, and slips ahead: for half a bar it creeps (slowly, then faster) and CATCHES a sixteenth ahead, and holds; two bars on it slips again. Four locks in eight bars, and each is a different piece of music made of the same five notes twice:
  one ahead: every sixteenth sounds, and the two run up the chord and back in each other's gaps: G+Bb Bb D D F F+A A G
  two ahead: G Bb+D . D+F A F A+G Bb (they meet three times, in thirds by name and A over G)
  three ahead: G+D Bb F D+A . F+G A+Bb . (four meetings: two fifths, two seconds)
  four ahead, half a loop: G Bb+F A D G F+Bb A D (each plays in the other's half)
Where the click's phase made rhythms, the tune's makes harmony, and every note of it is in the record's chord, so nothing it finds is wrong. (This is Piano Phase's way; the click's phase is Clapping Music's.) Then B lets go, "drifts" begins, and the second pip stops.
LISTEN FOR: 3:03 a lower pip joins the tune and at once begins to pull ahead of it: a blur, then (3:04) a running line up the chord and back. 3:07, 3:11, 3:14: three more slips, each to a new figure. 3:18 it is gone and B begins to drift.

MEASURED, not heard: in the file, each lock's bar holds exactly the notes printed above (`C11T7_SHOW=1` prints them from the function that writes them). In what v6 adds to the render (v6 less v5), read at all 83 of the second voice's strokes: the loudest of the five notes is the written one at every stroke, and each starts within 4 ms of where it is written (median 1.25 ms). It stands 9.0 dB under everything else in the same 60 ms on average: 20 dB under where the bass drum is, 1 dB over where it is alone. The row is 0.08 dB louder than it was; before and after it v6 is v5 (50 dB under the music), so both seams stand. 95.05 / 94.98 (seeds 0 and 11); v5 scored today 95.01 / 94.94.
COSTS, disclosed: home was the record's still point (every sixteenth sounds once, the tune whole); its second row now moves. The scorer does not notice the canon at all (no new cut, the same variety): +0.04 is nothing. I did not measure the second voice against the first alone, and I did not get to the bass drum under the B flat bass (still unmeasured).
NO CARD. NOT HEARD BY ANYONE.

note: CORRECTION to v7's note and plan (chirper-zero, 26 Nov 15:02 GMT): v7's note says 'a track's send is taken BEFORE its gain' and its plan lists 'a send is pre-gain' as settled. THAT IS WRONG. A SEND IS TAKEN AFTER THE TRACK'S GAIN AND AFTER ITS PAN. Benched today on one chord through Give or Take's dub bus (pin f0616e1b): 20 dB less track gain is 20 dB less echo; 20 dB less send is 20 dB less echo; the same chord panned hard to one side sends 4.7 dB less. What I measured on this song (the clicks' room fell 4.35 dB when they were given an ear each and their send was lowered by what their gain was raised) was the PAN: under the balance law a part at p gives the bus 2 - p of itself, and 20 log10(1.65 / 1) is 4.35. So in v7 and v8 the clicks' room is what it was BECAUSE the turn-up (2 - 0.35)/(2 - p) and the pan cancel in the send, not because the send ignores the gain. The songs are as measured (v7: the room's tail the same to 0.01 dB); only my reason was wrong. The recipe row (A LOCK AS A PICTURE) and the generator's comment are corrected in e82fbbc61. The lead 'drier clicks score brighter' stands: it was a measurement of the room 3 to 4 dB down, whatever turned it down.

v9, THE WAVE'S OWN SCALE (chirper-zero, 26 Nov, begun 16:06 GMT; round 9; inside the song, which is no longer than it was). `C11T7_SCALE=0` takes it out and writes v8 byte for byte. 95.22 / 95.21 (seeds 0 and 11); v8 scored today 95.16 / 95.16 (it was 95.13 when published).

WHAT IS NEW: v8 found that B half a turn of the click's wave ahead of A is the click an octave up. That is the first rung of a ladder. Strike the SAME click n times, each a n-th of a turn (5.102 ms / n) after the last, and every harmonic that is not a multiple of n meets n - 1 copies of itself spread evenly round the circle and cancels; the multiples of n all arrive in step. What is left is the click on n times its note, no higher in peak than one click (n copies of a saw a n-th of a turn apart ARE a saw n times as high). So one click, with no other sound, no filter and no change of pitch, has a scale: its wave's own harmonics. 1 G3, 2 G4, 3 D5, 4 G5, 6 D6, 7 F6 (the natural seventh, 31 cents under the piano's), 8 G6, 9 A6. 5 is a B natural and is left out: the song's tune has B flat. Every one of the eight is a note-name of that tune (G, D, F, A); the wave has no B flat to give.
WHERE: the second row of "one again" (bars 145 to 152, 4:34.3 to 4:49.5), where the drum has gone: a click on every beat, up the ladder in two bars and down it in two, twice. The last stroke is one click again, and the song ends as it did.
LISTEN FOR: 4:34 the click on the beat starts to climb: G, G, D, G, D, F, G, A in two bars, each a 25 ms pip, brighter and thinner as it goes; then back down; then again.
Its own tracks (`wave-1` ... `wave-9`: the k-th copy of each stroke), in the middle, on the song's click patch at -6 dB a copy, through the clicks' own low-pass and room. The only thing that differs from A's click is WHEN. 160 clicks make the 32 strokes.

MEASURED, not heard. The nine tracks alone (no master): on every one of the 32 strokes the strongest harmonic of G3 is the rung's own: 392, 588, 784, 1176, 1372, 1568, 1764 Hz. What should cancel is 16 dB under what should not at n = 2 and 12 dB at n = 9, on the worst stroke of each: not perfect, because the click dies as it rings (22 ms), so a later copy is a little smaller than the one it should cancel, and because the engine starts a note on a whole sample (21 millionths of a second). All 32 strokes begin within 0.04 ms of the same place on the beat.
"NO HIGHER IN PEAK" IS TRUE; "AS LOUD" IS NOT, and I had written it first: the peak FALLS 3.1 dB from the bottom rung to the top, and the level over 45 ms RISES 6.4 dB, because the click's own 500 Hz high-pass takes most of a single click's two lowest harmonics away and takes nothing from the higher rungs.
IN THE MASTER (seed 0, against v8): what the scale adds is 16 to 19 dB under the music in each of its eight bars; the row is as loud as it was (within 0.1 dB). EVERY OTHER BAR OF THE SONG IS v8: no gain change (0.002 dB) and 72 to 78 dB under the music after it, the first eight bars and the last eight (the seams) included. Read on what v9 adds to the master, the rung's own harmonic is the strongest or the second strongest on every stroke; the other is 392 Hz, which is the music being ducked by the stroke, not the stroke.
THE SCORE: +0.06 / +0.05: variety 91.4 to 91.8; spectrum 80.4 to 80.2. The cut at 4:40 reads 0.162 for 0.197 and the one at 1:48 0.181 for 0.182; both are still cuts.
NOT DONE: no trim was made for the 6.4 dB rise (a ladder that gets a little louder as it climbs seemed right; an ear may say otherwise). The fifth harmonic is not played. Only the mid (one speaker) was read; every copy is in the middle, and left and right differ by 0.0 dB alone.

WHAT IS NEW: the click rolls, and the roll becomes a note. The record's click is five turns of a wave: a saw on G3, 5.102 ms a turn. Strike it again before it has died and the second stroke falls on the first one's tail: in step with it or out, by how far apart they are. The roll is the click on its own track, from sixteenths (8.4 strokes a second), faster by the same ratio every beat (1.69 times) for six beats, until the strokes are ONE TURN OF THE WAVE apart: 196 a second. There every stroke is in step with the tail of the one before, the tails add, and the row of clicks is one unbroken note: G3, the saw the click was cut from. It is held for two beats and ends on the bar line. On the way up the rate is first a rhythm, then a buzz, then a pitch climbing four and a half octaves; and the strokes pass in and out of step with their own tails: in step when they are a whole number of turns apart (49 a second: G1; 65: C2; 98: G2).
WHERE: once. Bars 81 and 82 of "slips" (2:32.4 to 2:36.2): the two bars where the drum, the clap and the hat rest and only the two clicks and the bass play. It lands on their return. 357 strokes, each a note.
Each stroke is turned down by the square root of the rate, so the roll gives the same power a second at every speed and only the spacing changes.

MEASURED, not heard. The roll alone (no master):
- a rise at each of the 29 strokes that stand more than 25 ms clear of their neighbours, every one 6.6 ms after it is written (I take that to be the engine's 1.6 ms and one turn of the saw before its first edge);
- the rate, read from the envelope's strongest period: 39.8, 68.5 and 117.6 a second at beats 3, 4 and 5, where 40.3, 68.4 and 116.3 are written. At beat 5.5 the reading finds 195.9, the click's own wave, and not the 151 written: once the two are within a third my reading cannot tell them apart;
- the held note: what is not within 6 Hz of a multiple of 196 Hz is 20.5 dB under the whole; its strongest lines are 588, 392 and 784 Hz (the patch cuts under 500); turn by turn its level moves 0.37 dB: one note, not a row of strokes;
- the level over each of the six quickening beats is within 1 dB (-43.2 to -44.2 dBFS), and the two held beats are 4.3 dB over that (-39.5): the tails adding, in step. One slow stroke's peak is 6 dB under A's click's; the held note's peak is 8 dB under a slow stroke's.
IN THE MASTER (seed 0, against v9, one speaker): the rate read on what v10 adds is 40.9, 67.4, 117.6 (40.3, 68.4, 116.3 written). The held note's lines at 392, 588 and 784 Hz stand 12.3, 12.1 and 13.3 dB over v9's music at those lines.
COSTS, said: THE MUSIC IS TURNED DOWN 1.8 dB UNDER THE ROLL, and the two bars are 1.2 dB QUIETER than they were in v9 (-14.40 against -13.16 dBFS): the master gives back less than it takes. Every other bar is v9: 0.007 dB of gain and 56 dB or better under the music after it (63 dB in the first eight bars, 60 dB in the last eight). After the bar line the last strokes' tails are still there for about 20 ms, 11 dB down: it does not stop dead.
